title: Raipur steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business is, and where the cash sits
**A re-roller buys billet or scrap, heats it, rolls TMT bars, and sells into construction demand; the margin is a thin conversion spread, not a product premium.** Cash is trapped in inventory and receivables, and the spread moves with billet and scrap prices, which the local trade press reports falling on weak demand [2]. So when a proposal lands, check the conversion spread and inventory days first; if the spread is thin and inventory is building, ask why before you look at the plant.

## What has changed now
**Chhattisgarh is running slower than India on both demand and power: GST collections +2.4% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], and electricity demand +6.7% against +9.5% [D].** Local mills are also reporting production disruption from power shortages and rising costs [3]. Nationally, IIP for NIC 24 is only +2.4% YoY [D] and Brent at $113/bbl sits above the $75–100 band [D], which lifts freight and power-linked costs. So when a proposal lands, check the unit's own power tie-up and tariff; if it buys from the grid at spot, ask for the last six months' power bills.

## Where the growth is
**The peers that are growing are branded, integrated TMT players, not standalone re-rollers: Steel Exchange India reports ~₹340 crore revenue in Q2 FY27, up ~45% YoY [6], and Rathi Steel reports over ₹200 crore, up over 30% YoY [7].** JSW Steel's Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 20% with gearing at 0.42 [5], and Scan Steels points to value-added TMT and margin expansion [4]. Pursue Raipur borrowers with own billet/ingot linkage, a brand with dealer pull, and a captive or contracted power source; avoid pure conversion job-workers and units selling unbranded bar on price alone.

## How to grow safely
**Structure for the working-capital cycle, not the plant: cash-flow-based limits against inventory and receivables, with a charge on stock and book debts.** Take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, quarterly GST returns, and monthly power bills; covenant a minimum conversion spread and a maximum inventory days. If gearing is already stretched, note that peer rating reports show gearing at 1.80x [10] and moderately high working-capital needs [11]; ask for the debt repayment schedule and promoter support before enhancing.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the local demand and power signals monthly: if GST growth in the state stays below India's, or power disruption reports continue [3], tighten.** If billet-scrap spreads compress further [2], cut limits on the weakest accounts. If a borrower's inventory days rise while sales fall, stop fresh disbursement and ask for the sales register. Rating reports are old (2023–24) [8][9][10][11], so treat them as background, not current.
